entries.topic: The foreign-press ban and the Al Jazeera law

claims.text: 8 Jan 2024 Supreme Court rejected FPA appeal; state: independent entry could endanger soldiers and disclose troop positions; escorted access permitted; FPA: ban 'for 95 days straight, is unprecedented'.

Second petition filed Sept 2024 with Israeli and international press groups; after an Oct 26 hearing the state said 'there is no basis to allow the entry of journalists – Israeli or foreign – into the Gaza Strip without accompaniment', citing risks, interference with operations and the remains of hostage Ran Gvili; ~25 escorted entries by Israeli journalists and 5 group entries by foreign journalists since late October.

Oct 2026: still no independent foreign entry; embeds tightly controlled, no interviews with Palestinians; decision on second petition postponed 'numerous times'; Federman (AP/FPA): 'We haven't really been able to get a straight answer'; Ginsberg: lack of access becoming 'normalized'; Weimers (RSF) asks what Israel is trying to hide; NPR's Anas Baba: 'we are no longer carrying this burden alone'; CPJ 189 killed in Gaza.

April 2024 law let PM and communications minister close foreign networks harming state security; Al Jazeera shut in Israel May 2024; extended Dec 2025 to 2027, usable outside emergencies, reduced judicial oversight; Netanyahu: Al Jazeera 'harmed Israel's security, actively participated in the October 7 massacre, and incited against Israeli soldiers'; Al Jazeera: 'slanderous accusations'; Israel destroyed its Gaza office in 2021.
